instruction: GUI-only requirement: Complete the task entirely in the launched ZBrush graphical user interface. Do not open Command Prompt, PowerShell, Terminal, or any shell; do not run ZScript files, Python, macros, or other helper scripts/code that directly generates or edits the deliverable files. Use only ZBrush native GUI tools, menus, brushes, and built-in export commands. Morph Target Three-State Export The opened `scene.obj` contains a ZBrush Tool whose first (and only) SubTool, named Head, is a smooth head-shaped ellipsoid polymesh at approximately 2000 quads (32 lat x 64 lon with triangle caps; Y stretched by 1.3). It has a single default polygroup, no UVs, and no polypaint. Using the opened OBJ in ZBrush, use the Morph Target feature to capture three discrete states of a cheek-dent sculpt, and export them to `C:\Users\user\Desktop\baseline.obj`, `C:\Users\user\Desktop\edited.obj`, and `C:\Users\user\Desktop\partial.obj`. All three must share identical vertex and face counts. The three exported OBJs must satisfy: - Each contains exactly one SubTool named Head, and all three share identical vertex and face counts. - `C:\Users\user\Desktop\baseline.obj` matches the input `scene.obj` vertex-for-vertex within 1e-5 BU. - `C:\Users\user\Desktop\edited.obj` differs from `C:\Users\user\Desktop\baseline.obj` by at least 0.04 BU at the maximum displacement vertex. - `C:\Users\user\Desktop\partial.obj` equals `C:\Users\user\Desktop\edited.obj` within 0.01 BU for every vertex with y > 0.2, and equals `C:\Users\user\Desktop\baseline.obj` within 0.01 BU for every vertex with y <= 0.2. - All three meshes are manifold.
